title: Migrate billing export to event-sourced usage aggregates with opaque offsets for idempotent invoice lines
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: Reconciliation and invoice accuracy are being undermined by our current export pipeline which materializes invoice lines from near-real-time aggregates. Out-of-order webhook retries, late-arriving meter pulses, DST shifts, and small fractional usage entries combine to create non-deterministic exports, duplicate adjustment lines, and opaque corrective credits for customers.

Proposal: Replace the existing ad-hoc aggregation/rollup step with an event-sourced usage aggregator and an export layer that emits opaque, monotonic offsets per customer-account+meter stream. Exports will be generated deterministically from the event store up to a stable watermark and will reference an opaque offset token instead of timestamps when assembling invoice lines. This enables: 
- Idempotent replay of export runs (replay any watermark -> same invoice lines)
- Deterministic split/merge of usage buckets across plan changes without fractional drift
- Clear audit trail from exported invoice line -> originating usage events

Design highlights: 
1) Event store ingestion: normalize meter pulses into immutable events with canonical fields (account_id, meter_key, usage_qty, seq_no, received_at_utc, source_id). Use a per-account sequence number to ensure deterministic ordering.
2) Aggregator: materialize fixed-length epoch aggregates (e.g., 1m / 15m) into an append-only aggregate store. Aggregates hold raw and billed quantities and a list of contributing event seq ranges.
3) Opaque offsets: an export watermark is a token referencing aggregate epoch sequence (account_id:epoch_id:seq_end_hash). The token is opaque to downstream systems but deterministic and monotonic.
4) Export runner: assemble invoice lines by reading aggregates up to a watermark token. Each exported line embeds the offset token and contributing event ranges in metadata. Exports are signed with a stable checksum to detect tampering.
5) Migration path: run event-sourced aggregator in shadow mode alongside current pipeline for 3 billing cycles; compare export diffs via a reconciliation job and produce a reconciliation report. Only flip to production after diffs are below tolerance and rollback tests pass.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Re-run of export with same watermark yields byte-identical invoice lines and signatures.
- Reconciliation report for shadow mode shows zero net-proration drift versus current pipeline for >98% of accounts, and documented reasons for remaining differences.
- Late-arriving usage and retries no longer create duplicate invoice lines; any corrections are packaged as single, explainable adjustment entries with clear event-range metadata.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Storage growth for event store: use TTL+compaction of old events once exported and reconciled.
- Performance of export runner under high QPS: optimize aggregate epoch size and parallelize per-customer export shards. Prototype benchmarks required.
- Downstream compatibility: Stripe/Netsuite export writer will need to accept the opaque offset token and new checksum field; coordinate with accounting (Confluence doc linked in attachments).
comments: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Billing, Platform, and Accounting. Agreed on event-sourced approach and opaque offsets. Action: Platform to prototype aggregate model.
2026-03-05: Spike results: per-account append-only sequences feasible. Prototype aggregator processes 1M events/minute on r5.xlarge equivalent. PR: github.com/redwood/infer/pull/4826 (spike).

2026-03-09: Design review with Accounting team. Agreed to include offset token and signed checksum in CSV/JSON export. Accounting requested reconciliation column mapping to Netsuite memo field. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-11: Added data retention proposal to mitigate storage growth. Decided on 90-day raw event retention with 2-year compacted aggregates.
